sentences.text: Appearance:
Ms Priyanka Tiwari -Advocate for the applicant.
Shri D.R. Vishwakarma - Government Advocate for the respond  ORDER

This is the second application filed by the applicant under Section 483 of Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for grant of regular bail, who is behind the bars since 10.12.2023 in connection with FIR/Crime No.485/2023 registered at Police Station Mandla, District Mandla (M.P.) for the offence punishable under Section 376(1) of IPC and Section 3/4 of POCSO Act.
His earlier bail application faced dismissal as got withdrawn.

Learned counsel for the applicant sanguinely submits that though the applicant has been implicated in the alleged offence saying that he had committed rape with the prosecutrix who was minor, below 18 years of age but as per the learned counsel, the statement of prosecutrix and her mother have been recorded and as per their statement, it is clear that though she has supported the case of prosecution and stated against the applicant but it can be inferred that it was a case of consent.
The manner in which the crime alleged to have been committed itself shows that it is virtually not possible that any injury would not come over the body of the prosecutrix in the alleged incident.
It is evident from the MLC report that no injury was noticed on the person of the prosecutrix nor any such opinion has been given by the doctor.

Learned counsel submits that although the prosecution has come-up with a case that the prosecutrix is NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:12717 2 MCRC-10448-2025 minor and for determination of her age, a birth certificate was filed but as per the statement of mother of prosecutrix recorded in the court she has stated that no birth certificate was ever prepared by them.

sentences.text: 1 On these premise, learned counsel implores that the applicant may be granted bail.

In contrast, learned counsel for the State submits that the prosecutrix has wholly supported the prosecution case and she remained consistent in her statements recorded under Section 161, 164 and even before the court.
Ergo, the application deserves outright dismissal.

Considering the overall facts and circumstances, particularly the fact that the applicant is an under-trial accused and is behind the bars since 10.12.2023 and the material witnesses have already been examined, however, without commenting on the merits of the case, the application is allowed.

It is directed that the applicant shall be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned for his appearance before the concerned Court on all such dates as may be fixed by that Court in this regard during the pendency of trial.
It is further directed that the applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 480(3) of BNSS.
Accordingly, this M.Cr.C. stands disposed of.
